test_title: PYST 8: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - English Language (Held On 02 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom:
“A brown study”

options.text: A study related to earth sciences

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. **Lost in thought or daydreaming**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"A brown study"** refers to a state of being lost in thought, contemplation, or daydreaming. (सोच में खोया हुआ) • **Example:** He sat by the window in a brown study, oblivious to everything around him. • It does not relate to physical objects or studies but rather describes a mental state of deep thought or reflection. (गहरी सोच) • **Example:** The professor often falls into a brown study while working on his research. • Hence, the idiom "A brown study" means **Lost in thought or daydreaming**. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Option 1: A room with brown furniture** (भूरे रंग के फर्नीचर वाला कमरा): This option refers to a physical description and is unrelated to the idiom. • **Example:** The living room was decorated with brown furniture, giving it a warm and cozy feel. • **Option 3: A plan for redecorating** (पुनः सजावट की योजना): This option suggests an idea related to interior design, which is incorrect in the context of the idiom. • **Example:** She shared her plan for redecorating the house with bright colors and modern furniture. • **Option 4: A study related to earth sciences** (पृथ्वी विज्ञान से संबंधित अध्ययन): This option implies a scientific study, which does not align with the meaning of the idiom. • **Example:** He pursued a study related to earth sciences to understand environmental changes better. 33:T651, The correct answer is** option 2.**
